description: Kejaat (muninga) is a southern African hardwood with golden to reddish-brown heartwood, valued for furniture, flooring, carving and joinery because it is stable and works easily.

hazards.summary: A 1949 South African report described asthma caused by breathing kejaat wood dust. We could not access the details of how it was confirmed, so treat this as a reported effect.
All wood dust is classified as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure. This applies to this wood like any other.

exposure_limits.note: Applies to wood dust generally; this species has no separate ACGIH value.

related_species_note: Related to African padauk (Pterocarpus soyauxii), which has its own page. 'Bloodwood' is also used for unrelated woods such as Brosimum rubescens; check the botanical name.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed kejaat (Pterocarpus angolensis) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Heartwood a warm golden brown to reddish brown with irregular darker reddish streaks; a band of pale greyish-cream sapwood along one edge. Straight to slightly interlocked grain, medium-coarse texture with visible open pores and a soft natural sheen. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of kejaat with golden to reddish-brown heartwood and a band of pale sapwood.
notes_internal: Ordman-1949 has PMID 15397784 but no DOI or abstract; testing method unknown, so level 3. Not listed in HSE-WIS30 rev1. Description and common names (incl. kiaat) are from general knowledge, not a cited Tier D source; verify. Image colour description not source-verified.
